use /lib
from /scope/project-directory import ProjectDirectoryScope

export scope RibbonScope:
    concept: {RibbonConcept}

concept RibbonConcept:
    pitch:
        The ribbon along the top of the main window: tabs, each holding the
        application's commands for one area of work in labelled groups.

    shape: {RibbonShape}

shape RibbonShape:
    description:
        A ribbon runs along the top of the window, using gpui-kit's Tab
        component with its default styling. Its tabs are, in order: Project,
        Code, Spec, Research, and Application. The window always opens on
        Project. Beneath the tabs, the selected tab's commands sit in groups.
        There is no raw output view and no toggle for one.

    groups:
        Each group has its title in muted text rotated -90deg (bottom to top)
        aligned along the left edge of the group naming what its commands have
        in common. The title sits on a strip with a slightly different
        background colour, at 12px, with generous padding either side of it
        within the strip. Groups sit side by side with no divider between
        them: each group's title strip is what marks where it starts.

        project:
            A "Project" group holds the button for the @{ProjectDirectoryScope}.

        code:
            Nothing yet.

        spec:
            A "Build" group holds "Build Spec", which runs `piton build`.

        research:
            Nothing yet.

        application:
            An "Appearance" group holds the "Dark mode" switch, and a
            "Preferences" group holds "Settings", which opens the settings
            window.

        A tab with no commands reads "No commands yet".

    commands:
        A command button shows a large icon above its label: a folder for the
        project, a hammer for Build Spec, and a gear for Settings. The project
        button reads "Open Project…" until a project is open, then the project's
        name. An on or off setting, like dark mode, is a switch rather than a
        button.

        A command's tooltip explains what it does rather than repeating its
        label, and gives its keyboard shortcut if it has one.

        A command can be marked primary. For now, every command is primary:
        Open Project, Build Spec, Dark mode, and Settings.

        A command that can't run is disabled, not hidden, and its tooltip
        says why: Build Spec is disabled until a project is open, and while the
        spec is building.

    height:
        The command area is the same height on every tab, even one with no
        commands, so the window beneath doesn't move when switching tabs.

    collapsing:
        The ribbon collapses, and expands again, with a chevron button at the
        right end of the ribbon, by double-clicking a tab, or with Ctrl+F1
        (Cmd+F1 on macOS). Whether it is collapsed is saved for the user and
        restored on the next launch.

        Collapsed, the tabs go away too. The ribbon becomes a single thin row
        holding every primary command, from all of the tabs, as small buttons:
        a small icon beside its label, and dark mode as a small switch. They
        keep the order of their tabs, with a thin vertical divider between the
        commands of one tab and the next, and keep their tooltips and disabled
        states. The chevron sits at the right end of the row. Every control in
        the row, the chevron and the dividers included, is vertically centred
        in it.

Each ribbon tab now has its own scope in the spec, and the code is split the same way. RibbonScope keeps the description that applies to the whole ribbon.

**Spec** (`spec/ui/components/ribbon/`):
- **`index.pi`:** `RibbonScope` keeps the pitch, description, group layout, the general rules for commands, height, and collapsing. A new tabs section references the five tab scopes in order, and the details about specific commands moved out to them.
- **`project-tab`:** `RibbonProjectTabScope`, the Project group with Open Project. It covers the folder icon, the label before and after a project is open, both tooltips, and the project picker it opens, including what happens on cancel or error.
- **`spec-tab`:** `RibbonSpecTabScope`, the Build group with Build Spec. It covers the hammer icon, running `piton build`, when it's disabled and what the tooltips say, the spinner, and the notifications for success, failure, and "Could not run".
- **`application-tab`:** `RibbonApplicationTabScope`, with Dark mode under Appearance and Settings under Preferences. It covers the dark mode switch and how the choice is saved, and the settings window with its Ctrl+, / Cmd+, shortcut.
- **`code-tab`** and **`research-tab`:** `RibbonCodeTabScope` and `RibbonResearchTabScope`, with no commands yet.
- **Which commands are primary:** each tab now marks its own.
- **Back-references:** the tab scopes say "the ribbon" in plain text rather than referencing RibbonScope, because importing it back would create a circular import.

`piton check` and `piton build check` pass. I also ran `piton build`, so the tab reference docs now exist under `.claude/reference/ui/components/ribbon/`.

**Code:** `src/ribbon.rs` became `src/ribbon/mod.rs` plus one module per tab:
- `project_tab.rs`, `code_tab.rs`, `spec_tab.rs`, `research_tab.rs` and `application_tab.rs` each hold their tab's command list, render its commands, and contain the actions they run (picking a project, building, switching dark mode).
- `mod.rs` keeps the tabs, the group layout and titles, collapsing, and the shared button style, and asks each tab for its commands.

Nothing visible changes. The build has no warnings, and the tests stand at 122 passed, 1 skipped (it needs the real harness), with the same palette test failing as before.
